elements.evidence: Section 15.5(b) warrants only that services will conform in all material respects to the Agreement's requirements; it does not impose a professional-and-workmanlike standard.

elements.evidence: Section 15.5(a) warrants that each deliverable and item of software will conform in all material respects to its documentation and specifications.

elements.evidence: Section 15.5 permits Ono to elect replacement of the nonconforming deliverable, software, or services.

result.reason: The operative language reaches the expressly stated fallback by providing 90-day software and 30-day services warranties with repair, replacement, and refund remedies. It does not reach the preferred position because it omits the professional-and-workmanlike, legal-compliance, and malicious-code warranties and uses shorter periods. The redline preserves the existing disclaimer because Section 15.4 expressly carves out warranties stated elsewhere. It is not strictly minimal because it additionally covers deliverables against specifications, beyond the fallback's stated software/documentation requirement. Drafting quality is reduced by awkwardly treating services as capable of being “replaced,” using the unclear antecedent “them” for refund calculations, and failing to state how refund amounts are allocated where deliverables, software, and services are bundled.
